63: // diff compares two multi-line strings and returns a helpful comment
64: func diff(got, want string) string {
65: 	g := strings.Split(got, "\n")
66: 	w := strings.Split(want, "\n")
67: 	for i := 0; ; i++ {
68: 		switch {
69: 		case i < len(g) && i < len(w):
70: 			if g[i] == w[i] {
71: 				continue
72: 			}
73: 			return fmt.Sprintf("-- first difference in line %d:\n"+
74: 				"-- got : %q\n-- want: %q\n", i+1, g[i], w[i])
75: 		case i < len(g):
76: 			return fmt.Sprintf("-- got %d extra lines after line %d:\n"+
77: 				"-- first extra line: %q\n", len(g)-len(w), i, g[i])
78: 		case i < len(w):
79: 			return fmt.Sprintf("-- got %d correct lines, want %d more lines:\n"+
80: 				"-- want next: %q\n", i, len(w)-i, w[i])
81: 		default:
82: 			return "no differences found"
83: 		}
84: 	}
85: }

All tests pass. I implemented the solution in `food_chain.go` without touching the test file or creating new files.

The approach is algorithmic, as the spec suggests:
- `animals` and `comments` are two parallel slices — the eight animals in order, and each animal's comment line.
- `Verse(v)` builds the verse with a `strings.Builder`: the intro line, the animal's comment, then a cumulative loop that walks backward through the chain emitting "She swallowed the X to catch the Y." lines (appending the spider's "that wriggled and jiggled..." detail when the spider is the prey). Verses 2–7 end with the concluding "Perhaps she'll die." line; the fly verse ends after its comment, and the horse verse ends with "She's dead, of course!".
- `Verses(start, end)` joins `Verse` results with a blank line, and `Song()` is `Verses(1, 8)`.

`go test ./...` reports `ok foodchain`.
